name: AlNahla Group | مجموعة النهلة
category: diversified holding conglomerate (investment / real estate / automotive / hospitality)
reason: Confirms prior OUT. Al Nahla is a Jeddah family holding conglomerate across five verticals: Investment, Real Estate, Trade (SAMACO Marine yachts/boats, SAMACO toys), Automotive (SAMACO Automotive dealerships, Fast Auto Technique), and Hospitality/F&B projects. Corporate press/about site only, no retail cart.

name: NANCO Group
reason: Confirms prior OUT. NANCO (formerly Al Nakhla Al Ahliah) is a Riyadh-founded transportation and logistics services company: ground transport since 1969, fuel-station services from 1995, and airport services from 2012. This is a services business, not retail.

name: مفارش العييري
reason: Confirms prior IN. Real, live e-commerce store for bedding, mattresses, pillows and padding with a broad multi-line catalog (not a single narrow SKU line), active discount codes, checkout, and free Kingdom-wide shipping. Bedding/pillows/mattress-protectors carry meaningfully higher repeat-purchase frequency than the confirmed narrow-fail patterns (lighting-only, flooring-only), so Gate 3 is passed. || CROSS-VERIFICATION (independent 2nd pass): Real live Saudi bedding retailer (Buraydah, Salla store plus iOS/Android apps), but independent checks could not confidently confirm Gate 3 breadth or Gate 5 scale: homepage is JS-rendered (blank category links on two fetches), the product sitemap returned 410 Gone, and multiple sources describe it as mattress/'comfortable sleep'-centric rather than broad soft-bedding. Genuine unresolved ambiguity on the narrow-category/scale gates.

name: Ali Zaid Al-Quraishi & Brothers
reason: Confirms prior OUT. AZAQ is a 100%-family-owned Saudi investment/holding group operating since 1958 across automotive & mobility, consumer goods, supply chain & logistics, industrial/tech solutions, real estate, and financial services. Pure corporate 'who we are' site, no retail storefront.

name: AlRashed Building Materials Co.
reason: Confirms prior OUT. Explicit construction building-materials supplier (sections & profiles, sheets & plates, pipes & tubes, deformed bars, wood-based panels, wood) serving contractors through 30+ branches. Hard-fail category regardless of scale or how live the operation is.

name: Al Rashed Tires
reason: Confirms prior OUT. OTR (off-the-road)/industrial tire and battery distributor explicitly targeting Dealers/Distributors/Fleet Owners/Manufacturers/OEMs/Trading Companies via a B2B registration form. Automotive tires/batteries are an explicit hard-fail category regardless of the (largely unused) shopping-cart scaffolding present on the theme.

name: Al Rawabi Group of Companies W.L.L
reason: Confirms prior IN. Al Rawabi Group's own corporate site (Doha, Qatar, since 1980) directly links its 'Retail' vertical to Rawabi Hypermarket, which is a large, live, transactional online grocery/hypermarket delivery platform with an enormous real SKU catalog and genuine QAR pricing -- the group also runs a Tasveek grocery-delivery app on iOS/Android. Qatar HQ is explicit, matching the row's country. || CROSS-VERIFICATION (independent 2nd pass): Gate 6 + Gate 4: this is the parent corporate/holding site of a conglomerate that mixes retail with wholesale (Rawabi Food International, Emdadco, Wholesale Plus), food manufacturing, distribution and hospitality. Mixed-conglomerate parent is excluded (only the hypermarket subsidiary, row #21, qualifies), and a holding page is not itself a storefront.

name: ALSAIF Trading Agencies Co.
category: wholesale distribution of housewares & electrical appliances (B2B)
reason: Reverses prior IN (home_furniture_appliance). Al Saif is a since-1962 housewares/electrical-appliance brand distributor whose own site explicitly tells consumers to buy through third-party channels ('أماكن الشراء: المتاجر الإلكترونية / المتاجر المتخصصة / الهايبرماركت / خدمة الجملة' -- e-stores, specialty stores, hypermarkets, wholesale service) rather than from Al Saif directly; they state they distribute through 1,300+ distributors. alsaifco.com itself has zero cart/price content -- just catalogs/PDFs and a 'join as distributor' page. A secondary alsaifco.sa (Zid-platform) subsite exists, but it is only a loyalty-points-redemption micro-store, not a general product storefront.

name: AlSaif Group
reason: Company is a transportation, logistics and real-estate development conglomerate (est. 1960), not a retailer; no consumer products sold on site.

name: Mohamed Naser Al-Sayer & Sons Establishment Company W.L.L.
reason: Kuwait's largest Toyota/Lexus automotive distributor and diversified conglomerate (feed manufacturing, beverages, F&B franchising); automotive dealer/distributor is a hard-fail category.

name: Marzooq S. Al Shamlan Holding
reason: Diversified Qatari holding group (automotive/tire trading, Karcher equipment, general trading) since 1950; corporate site has no cart/checkout of its own.

name: Alshareef for building materials
reason: B2B building-materials importer (bricks, rebar, timber) since 1975; explicitly excluded construction-materials category.

name: Alsourayia Trading Co.
category: flooring_carpet (narrow home-goods specialty, not diversified trading)
reason: Live e-commerce site, but sells only flooring and carpets (vinyl/parquet/SPC flooring, office/mosque/hotel carpets, artificial grass); matches the explicitly confirmed narrow-category fail pattern of 'flooring/carpet only'.

name: IKEA Alsulaiman
reason: IKEA Alsulaiman is operated by Ghassan Alsulaiman Furniture Trading Co. (Alsulaiman Group), a genuinely Saudi-HQ'd conglomerate holding the exclusive IKEA franchise for Saudi Arabia and Bahrain since 1983 (the first-ever IKEA franchise globally) - this is exactly the 'Saudi conglomerate that owns the local IKEA franchise rights' pattern that passes Gate 1 despite IKEA being a foreign brand. It operates 11 stores in-Kingdom plus Bahrain across the broad home/furniture/general-merchandise category (Gate 2/3 pass, not narrow). Its site is a fully functioning e-commerce operation with cart/checkout, financing (0% installments via Al Rajhi Bank, SNB, Tamara) and same-day/free-delivery thresholds, spanning dozens of product categories (Gate 4/5 pass). || CROSS-VERIFICATION (independent 2nd pass): Gate 6 fail. alsulaimangroup.com is the mixed-conglomerate parent, blending IKEA/retail with logistics, real estate, automotive leasing and contracting; mixed parents are excluded, and the IKEA retail arm would need its own row on the IKEA store domain rather than this holding page.

name: السلطان | AlSultan
reason: Live e-commerce site, but sells only bedding/linens (bedspreads, blankets, prayer rugs, hotel pillows), a single narrow home-textile product line with lower repeat-purchase frequency, analogous to the confirmed flooring/carpet-only fail pattern.

name: ALTAWKILAT
reason: Major Saudi automotive distributor (Maserati, Infiniti, Chevrolet, GMC, Dongfeng, Hongqi) under Tawad Holding; explicitly excluded automotive category. Domain currently redirects to a Bitly branded-domain landing page (parked/expired), but the underlying business is unambiguously automotive.

name: Al Waha For Cars
reason: Qatar car dealership (Jetour showrooms, cars for sale/rent, service centers); explicitly excluded automotive category.

name: Al Wajba Motors
reason: Exclusive Qatar dealer for Bentley, Lamborghini, Bugatti and McLaren; explicitly excluded luxury automotive category.

name: Al Wazzan Group of Companies
reason: Kuwaiti diversified holding group of 30+ companies (real estate, healthcare, automotive/Ford Kuwait, retail and distribution, construction); the live site is also a defunct placeholder page with no real retail content.

name: Alwazzan United Trading company
reason: Kuwait-HQ'd (est. 1975, Shuwaikh/Hawally addresses, +965 numbers) home fit-out company selling bespoke kitchens, built-in wardrobes, doors and luxury safes on an appointment/consultation basis. Even granting it 'home/furniture' category, it fails the repeat-purchase test: fitted kitchens, wardrobes, doors and safes are one-time, project-based home fixtures, the same low-frequency pattern as the confirmed 'flooring/carpet only' fail, and the site has no cart or pricing at all, only 'Book an Appointment'.

name: شركة اليحيا Alyahya Company
reason: Thin, dated (copyright 2011) corporate site listing Cars, Automotive Service, Spare Parts, Apiaries, Nurseries and Realty as the company's activities. None of these are approved retail categories; automotive and real estate are explicit hard-fail categories, and apiaries/nurseries are agriculture, not retail.

name: Alymama اليمامة
reason: Genuine Saudi-HQ'd (Riyadh, Ministry of Commerce CR registered Dec 2014) e-commerce operation with real SAR pricing and cart, but the entire catalog is a single narrow accessory line: watches (about 20 face/strap color variants) plus 3 leather belts. This is a one-product-type accessory shop, not multi-item fashion, and watches/belts carry inherently low repeat-purchase frequency similar to jewelry.

name: Hassan Misfer Al-Zahrani & Partners Group
reason: This is 'Al Zahrani Holding', a Saudi industrial/trading conglomerate, not a retailer. Its listed operating subsidiaries are Al Zahrani Trading, Taziz General Trading, Al Zahrani Trading & Contracting, Trans Peninsula Trading (cargo), Trans Saudi Travel & Tour, Mansour Stainless Steel Fabricators, and Al Zahrani Industrial Maintenance/Engineering. None of these are a qualifying retail category (contracting, cargo, travel and industrial maintenance are all excluded); the site is a legacy Flash-based page with no storefront. This corrects the prior 'general_merch_dept' categorization, which does not match the actual business found on the live site.

name: Amazon KSA Markets
reason: The domain returned an anti-bot 'checking your browser' challenge page, and WebSearch confirms the actual official Amazon Saudi Arabia storefront is amazon.sa (the Souq.com successor), not this domain. Regardless of which exact domain is used, the underlying operating entity is Amazon.com Inc., globally headquartered in Seattle, USA, not Saudi Arabia, so this fails geography outright even though Amazon has substantial real operations in the Kingdom.
